The procedure defines the future workflow for producing and reviewing OperationProposal records while preserving protected-path, human-gate, and professional-boundary constraints, and does not activate domain-engine operation execution.
Prerequisite: an accepted future amendment authorizing domain-engine operation workflow implementation is TBD.
Prerequisite: an accepted DomainEngineProfile for the target engine is TBD.
Prerequisite: protected path and proposal path policy is TBD, in sibling deliverable DEL-10-02.
Prerequisite: a deterministic adapter or validation tool for the operation is TBD.
Prerequisite: an explicit human gate definition and acceptance evidence format is TBD.
Step 1: Confirm future-boundary authorization, verifying work remains proposal/workflow design unless a governed amendment authorizes implementation.
Step 2: Create a draft OperationProposal record, populating each required field from docs/TYPES.md Section 11.2 and using TBD for unavailable values.
Step 2: Keep ResponsibleParty outside the proposal workflow as TBD until human assignment.
Step 3: Identify inputs and intended changes, filling inputRefs and intendedChanges and not writing directly to protected domain-engine model truth.

Step 4: Define deterministic checks in deterministicChecks, marking exact check payloads, pass/fail schema, adapter/profile reference, evidence path, and failure reason as TBD until an adapter/profile contract is accepted.
Step 5: Identify expected outputs and risks, populating expectedOutputRefs with proposal/review artifacts or approved future adapter outputs and using TBD for risks needing domain expert review.

Step 6: Set the required human gate by populating requiredHumanGate or marking it TBD, keeping acceptance artifact format, actor/authority, timestamp rule, and proposal binding TBD, and not moving to application without explicit human acceptance.

Step 7: Review protected-path and professional-boundary posture, confirming agents write only proposals/summaries/review aids and that text claims no professional approval, code compliance, external validation, or Chirality-owned solver truth.
Step 8: Status draft means an initial incomplete or working proposal.
Step 8: ASSUMPTION ready_for_review means required fields are populated or marked TBD, deterministic checks are prepared, and unresolved blockers are visible in the review checklist.
Step 8: ASSUMPTION accepted means explicit human acceptance has been recorded in a future acceptance evidence artifact bound to the proposal identifier.
Step 8: ASSUMPTION rejected means a human reviewer or policy rejects the proposal and records the rejection reason in the same evidence family as acceptance.
Step 8: ASSUMPTION applied means an approved future adapter applies the operation after human acceptance and records adapter validation/apply results.
Human ruling is needed before these status transition semantics become implementation requirements.

The deliverable defines a future-boundary data model and review workflow for OperationProposal records, covering proposal record shape, required human-gate posture, and review checklist for future domain-engine operations.
The deliverable excludes current-release domain operation execution, domain adapter implementation, protected-path enforcement implementation, and any claim that Chirality owns solver truth.

REQ-10-03-001: the future operation proposal record MUST include the OperationProposal fields proposalId, profileId, operationName, createdAt, createdBy, inputRefs, intendedChanges, deterministicChecks, expectedOutputRefs, risks, requiredHumanGate, and status.
REQ-10-03-002: status values MUST remain draft, ready_for_review, accepted, rejected, and applied unless amended through governed change.
REQ-10-03-003: domain operations MUST be represented as OperationProposal records before application.
REQ-10-03-004: applying a domain operation MUST require explicit human acceptance.
REQ-10-03-005: proposal records MUST identify inputs, intended changes, deterministic checks, expected outputs, risks, and required human gates.
REQ-10-03-006: agents MUST write proposals, summaries, and review aids, not protected domain-engine model truth.
REQ-10-03-007: domain-engine outputs MUST NOT be represented as professional approval, code compliance, external validation, or solver truth owned by Chirality.
REQ-10-03-008: ASSUMPTION a proposal should not reach applied status without a successful deterministic adapter/application workflow and recorded human acceptance.
REQ-10-03-009: human acceptance evidence MUST remain a named TBD implementation blocker until the artifact format, actor/authority field, timestamp rule, and proposal identifier binding are defined.

REQ-10-03-010: deterministic check evidence MUST remain a named TBD implementation blocker until the result payload, pass/fail semantics, adapter/profile reference, and provenance location are defined.

REQ-10-03-011: review sufficiency evidence MUST identify a future review-checklist artifact recording schema completeness, boundary-language review, protected-path posture, human-gate status, and unresolved TBD blockers.
